subject: EU-West rolling driver handoff advisory — short restarts with KV warm-preserve plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudverse.com>, ops@cloudverse.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU-West rolling driver handoff advisory — short restarts with KV warm-preserve plan

Hi Aisha / Cloudverse ops team,

We wanted to let you know about a scheduled maintenance window in eu-west (multiple AZs) where we'll perform a rolling driver/kernel handoff and apply a small safety patch to the compute host drivers that improves stability for long-lived KV caches. High-level:

- Window: May 11, 2028 01:00 - 05:00 UTC (we expect work to be concentrated in the first 3 hours)
- Expected customer impact: per-host service process restart ~2-5 minutes during each host's maintenance; we’ll preserve KV cache where possible and pre-warm replicas to reduce cold-starts, but some requests may experience higher latency or transient 503s while traffic migrates.
- Scope: rolling across AZs to avoid region-wide disruption; burst capacity will be used to maintain throughput.
- Why: a driver-level fix addresses a rare latency spike under sustained KV cache pressure and reduces risk of prolonged evictions.

Operational notes and recommended actions for Cloudverse:
- If you have heavy batch jobs or bulk ingestion between 01:30–03:30 UTC, consider rescheduling to outside the core window.
- We recommend setting client retry with exponential backoff for 30s and increasing request timeout to 60s for streaming requests during the window.
- We will post live updates to the status page and provide a runbook link; our on-call will be monitoring traces and token-level latency.

Attachments: euw-rolling-runbook.pdf (runbook, rollback steps), euw-node-map.csv (host/AZ mapping).

If you want us to shift the start, let us know by EOD tomorrow and we can coordinate. Otherwise we'll proceed and circle back with a post-run summary and any follow-up actions.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Account Reliability
Redwood Inference
mobile: +1-415-555-0110

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudverse.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cloudverse.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-West rolling driver handoff advisory — short restarts with KV warm-preserve plan

Thanks for the heads up, Sean — appreciate the detail. A couple quick questions from our side: 

1) Our heaviest ingestion runs are between 02:00–03:00 UTC (daily). Can you confirm whether the rolling schedule will touch the host pool that handles that workload during that hour?

2) If we see elevated error rates, who should we escalate to? We need a direct SRE contact for our on-call to page.

If shifting start by a couple hours reduces risk to us, we’d prefer it — we have an important batch that cannot be easily moved.

— Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Cloud Ops, Cloudverse
aisha.khan@cloudverse.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudverse.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-West rolling driver handoff advisory — scheduling tweak request

On Tue, 09 May 2028 at 09:12, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> We wanted to let you know about a scheduled maintenance window in eu-west ...

Sean — Cloudverse flagged their critical ingestion between 02:00–03:00 UTC. We have capacity buffers but to be conservative I propose shifting the start later by 2 hours to 03:00 UTC so the Cloudverse window is outside the busiest part of our rolling schedule. That would move the window to 03:00–07:00 UTC. Priyom, can the ops team accommodate that shift without impacting other high-priority tenants that requested earlier windows?

I’ve reviewed the runbook; rollback path A (quick-driver-revert + warm-restart) looks safe and takes ~10 minutes for affected host if we need it. We should also ensure we have the KV-prefill job primed 15 minutes before the start in each AZ we touch. I can own the pre-warm trigger for Cloudverse AZs.

— Monica
Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudverse.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 11:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-West rolling driver handoff advisory — updated start time confirmed

Thanks — we can shift the start as requested. Final plan:

- New window: May 11, 2028 03:00 - 07:00 UTC.
- We will sequence maintenance so AZ-A -> AZ-B -> AZ-C; each host restart expected 2–5 minutes, with a safety hold of 10 minutes between AZs.
- Priyom (ops) will run KV-prefill 15 minutes ahead of each AZ work, Monica will validate pre-warm signals for Cloudverse slices.
- On-call: Priyom Das (priops@redwood.com) primary, backup Monica Patel (monica_patel@redwood.com). If Cloudverse wants direct paging, provide the number for their on-call and we’ll add a 3-way bridge.

We’ll post live updates on the status page and share a short postmortem within 48 hours after the run with metrics (errors, token-latency delta, cache hit ratio).

Sean — I’ll update the runbook link and notify other tenants of the small schedule tweak.

— Priyom
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
